guide.line: John Muir came to America from Scotland as an eleven-year-old farm boy in 1849 and grew into the most persuasive voice for keeping wild country wild.
guide.copy_md_sentence: John Muir came to America from Scotland as an eleven-year-old farm boy in 1849 and grew into the most persuasive voice for keeping wild country wild.

guide.line: In 1849 his family emigrated to the United States and settled on Wisconsin farmland — first at Fountain Lake, then at Hickory Hill Farm near Portage.
guide.copy_md_sentence: In 1849 his family emigrated to the United States and settled on Wisconsin farmland — first at Fountain Lake, then at Hickory Hill Farm near Portage.

guide.line: In 1860 he carried his inventions to the state fair in Madison, won prizes and notice, and entered the University of Wisconsin.
guide.copy_md_sentence: In 1860 he carried his inventions to the state fair in Madison, won prizes and notice, and entered the University of Wisconsin.

guide.line: He left after about three years without a degree, having fallen for botany and geology, and wandered the northern states and Canada doing odd jobs along the way.
guide.copy_md_sentence: He left after about three years without a degree, having fallen for botany and geology, and wandered the northern states and Canada doing odd jobs along the way.

guide.line: In 1868 he sailed by way of Cuba and Panama, crossed the isthmus, and came up the coast to San Francisco in March.
guide.copy_md_sentence: In 1868 he sailed by way of Cuba and Panama, crossed the isthmus, and came up the coast to San Francisco in March.

guide.line: For years Muir read the Sierra's glaciers, meadows and storms at first hand, and in 1874 his "Studies in the Sierra" began a long career as a writer who could make a reader feel a landscape they had never seen.
guide.copy_md_sentence: For years Muir read the Sierra's glaciers, meadows and storms at first hand, and in 1874 his "Studies in the Sierra" began a long career as a writer who could make a reader feel a landscape they had never seen.

guide.line: Writing, for Muir, was a way of defending what he loved.
guide.copy_md_sentence: Writing, for Muir, was a way of defending what he loved.

guide.line: In 1890, after a campaign Muir fought alongside the editor Robert Underwood Johnson, an act of Congress created Yosemite National Park; the National Park Service dates it precisely to 1 October 1890.

guide.line: In 1880 he married Louie Strentzel, settled in Martinez, California, raised two daughters, and ran the family fruit ranch.

guide.line: The two slipped away from the official party into the back country for several days; Roosevelt went home and threw the weight of the presidency behind protecting the nation's forests, parks and monuments.
